---
pagetitle: "Peekbank | Data Access"
title: "Data access"
---

Peekbank data live in two versioned, public datasets on
[Redivis](https://redivis.com/datapages):
[**peekbank**](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank) (the
relational tables) and
[**peekbank_files**](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank_files)
(raw data, processed intermediates, stimuli, and per-dataset READMEs).
Access requires a free Redivis account; the first request from any client
opens a browser window to authorize (or set a `REDIVIS_API_TOKEN`).

## R: peekbankr (recommended)

```r
install.packages("redivis", repos = "https://langcog.r-universe.dev", type = "source")
remotes::install_github("peekbank/peekbankr")
```

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(peekbankr)

con <- connect_to_peekbank()   # pins the current release; prints which one

aoi_timepoints <- get_aoi_timepoints(connection = con, dataset_name = "pomper_saffran_2016")
administrations <- get_administrations(connection = con, dataset_name = "pomper_saffran_2016")

ps_data <- aoi_timepoints %>% left_join(administrations)
```

Accessors: `get_datasets()`, `get_subjects()`, `get_administrations()`,
`get_trials()`, `get_trial_types()`, `get_stimuli()`,
`get_aoi_region_sets()`, `get_aoi_timepoints()`, `get_xy_timepoints()`,
plus `unpack_aux_data()` for the JSON aux columns (CDI scores etc.),
`download_stimuli()` and `get_readmes()` for files, and `get_sql_query()`
for arbitrary SQL. Full reference:
[peekbank.github.io/peekbankr](https://peekbank.github.io/peekbankr/).

### Versions

Peekbank is released in named versions. `connect_to_peekbank()` uses the
latest release by default and announces it; pin any release for
reproducibility:

```r
con <- connect_to_peekbank(db_version = "2025.1")
get_db_info()   # lists all available versions
```

The Redivis-hosted versions correspond to the historical releases 2021.1,
2022.1, 2025.1, 2025.2, and 2026.1 (2021.1 and 2022.1 contain identical
data; both are kept for citation stability).

## Python and other languages

The [redivis-python](https://apidocs.redivis.com/client-libraries/redivis-python)
client reads the same tables:

```python
import redivis

ds = redivis.organization("datapages").dataset("peekbank")
datasets = ds.table("datasets").to_pandas_dataframe()
aoi = ds.query("""
  SELECT * FROM aoi_timepoints_rle
  WHERE administration_id IN (
    SELECT administration_id FROM administrations WHERE dataset_id = 25)
""").to_pandas_dataframe()
```

Pin versions with `dataset("peekbank", version="v1.2")`; each version's
`release_info` table names the Peekbank release it holds. You can also
query, explore, and export every table interactively on the
[Redivis dataset page](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank).

## SQL

Redivis datasets are queryable with standard (BigQuery-dialect) SQL — in
the browser via each dataset's *Query* tab, or through the clients as
above. Note for users of the retired MySQL server: string comparison is
now case-sensitive, and the `aoi_timepoints_indexed` helper table no
longer exists (`aoi_timepoints_rle` remains).

## Raw data and stimuli

Every dataset's raw eye-tracking exports, processed peekds CSVs, stimulus
images/audio, and README are files in
[peekbank_files](https://redivis.com/datapages/datasets/peekbank_files),
named by path (`<dataset>/raw_data/...`, `<dataset>/processed_data/...`,
`<dataset>/README.md`). Use `peekbankr::download_stimuli()` /
`get_readmes()`, or browse and download from Redivis directly.

dataset you use (listed on the [Datasets](datasets.html) page, with the
database release you used, e.g. "Peekbank 2026.1"):
